text:
Alice PM: Quick sync — we need to align on customer contract language + network ops constraints for the next private deploy sprint. Goal: agree launch gates by EOD Thu.
Ben NetEng: Top concerns I see: IP preservation during peering changes, upgrade window coordination, and whether we accept customer-managed NAT.
Carla Sales: From field: customers keep bringing up pricing buckets tied to reserved IPs and slow upgrades. They want a clear SLA and a pricing waiver if we do a forced downtime >30m.
Dmitri Eng: Technical reality: we can support non-disruptive agent rollouts for most instances, but if customers own routing and swap subnets, we need a handshake and migration operator.
Elena FieldSE: Can we put a hard launch gate: "customer network ownership acknowledged + contact + IP preservation plan signed"? That helps legal and netops.
Carla Sales: Yes — propose clause: `Customer is responsible for customer-managed routing and peering. Redwood will provide migration playbook and 2x maintenance windows per week; any emergency migration outside windows may incur SLA credits.` Thoughts?
Ben NetEng: That clause is ok but add: `Customer must preserve source/destination IP mapping during cutover or provide translation plan.` Without that, log continuity breaks.
Dmitri Eng: Implementation note: our installer can emit a preflight report: `net-check.json` with ASN, CIDRs, NAT behaviour. Field can require that artefact as a condition of booking the upgrade window.
Elena FieldSE: Preflight report is great. Make it a launch gate item in the acceptance checklist: preflight present + handoff to NetOps.
Alice PM: Draft launch gates idea: 1) Signed network appendix 2) preflight report uploaded 3) scheduled maintenance window confirmed 4) rollback plan accepted 5) pricing/credits acknowledged. Anyone object?
Carla Sales: Add one more: 6) Customer contact for L2/L3 changes (direct Slack/phone) in the booking.
Ben NetEng: Also need a "fallback route" policy — how we fall back if peering breaks. Suggest we require a fallback route or documented plan.
Dmitri Eng: Agree. For upgrades, we should support staged canary with `--staged-agent` flag; if canary fails, auto-rollback to previous image. Ops-bot can handle the webhook.
ops-bot: Deploy hook template created: `/hooks/upgrade-canary` — includes `rollback_on_fail:true` and `notify:#oncall`.
Elena FieldSE: Field checklist for customers (short): network appendix, preflight, accepted windows, contact, fallback route, test traffic plan. We'll put this in the onboarding packet.
Carla Sales: On pricing: teams want a discount for multi-tenant reserved IPs vs ephemeral. Can Legal weigh in? If we offer credits for outages, we must bind those to clear thresholds.
Dmitri Eng: Technically we can measure outage duration via agent heartbeat + control-plane logs. We should define metrics: control_plane_unavailable_seconds and agent_data_plane_drop_rate.
Alice PM: OK action items: - Carla: draft network appendix + SLA clause by tomorrow. - Ben: write preflight schema + required fields (`cidrs`, `nat_behavior`, `peering_method`) - Dmitri: add `--staged-agent` rollback flow + ops-bot webhook - Elena: make 1-pager for field + add launch gates to checklist.
Carla Sales: I'll also push one example contract blurb: "Redwood may perform upgrades within agreed windows; Customer to provide network contact and preserve IP mappings; outage credits apply if downtime >30m outside approved maintenance."
Ben NetEng: One more: define acceptable maintenance windows cadence (e.g., local-business hours allowed? we need to be explicit per region). Add as part of the appendix.
Alice PM: Timeline: draft items by tomorrow, review Thu morning, sign-off Thu EOD. If anyone can't meet that, call it out now.
Elena FieldSE: I can review Carla's draft midday and validate the preflight fields.
Dmitri Eng: I'll open a PR for the staged-agent flow today, pinging @Ben for net-check integration.
Carla Sales: Noted. I'll ping Legal after I have the appendix draft.
Ben NetEng: :thumbsup: I'll sketch the `net-check.json` schema in the PR body.
Alice PM: Great. If no blockers, we'll lock these launch gates and add to the private-deploy checklist for the sprint. Thanks everyone.
Elena FieldSE: Quick Q — what about air-gapped installs where we can't run ops-bot? We need alternate handshake flow.
Dmitri Eng: For air-gapped: we can generate the preflight package offline and the customer uploads the signed package. Add that as an exception in the checklist.
Carla Sales: I'll call that out in the appendix as an "airgap flow" with separate acceptance criteria.
Alice PM: Perfect. Closing thread — I'll post updated checklist after reviews. :sparkles:
